long_description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent cancer forms with close to 2 million new cases per year worldwide. Each year approximately 800.000 patients die of their CRC. The gold standard for diagnosis of CRC is colonoscopy, targeting polyps, abnormal tissue growths that may evolve into cancer. Early disease detection has a significant impact on mortality from colorectal cancer, going from a high 5-year survival probability of 90% if detected early, to a low 10-30% 5-year survival probability in later stages. Studies have shown that up to 40% of polyps can be missed during colonoscopies. Large variations in detection rates are also observed between physicians. To remedy the variability in detection rates, there is a high medical need for tools to improve detection of polyps in colonoscopy. Such tools can save lives and reduce the treatment costs for hospitals and society by preventing CRC cases due to early detection. Based on more than 10 years of research conducted at Simula Research Laboratory, we are developing, documenting and commercializing an AI-powered digital health system that can detect polyps in real-time during a colonoscopy examination without interruption of the procedure. The device is connected to the video output of standard endoscopy equipment and provides feedback on visible lesions to the performing doctor overlaid on their examination screen. long_description: Why we’re here In 2017, when we looked at available secure communications technology, we saw products technologically incapable to deal with advanced adversaries, and products challenged by the involvement of Nation State Actors. We saw a need for a different kind of technology, and we knew it would take a different kind of company to build it. That’s why we founded ARMA Instruments. ARMA is an acronym to Advanced Relay Mission Applications. Challenges we solve You cannot prevent espionage on just the software level using encryption or even quantum resilient encryption. An attacker may tap into system vulnerabilities hidden in files or applications, hidden in operating system components, or perhaps in the many hardware components. The more convenience a system offers, the more complex it gets, giving room for many different angles of attack. This way, the encryption is already compromised before it has even come to effect. All system layers in a communications solution need to be secured, from the applications and software to the operating system and hardware platform. Our mission To provide absolute communications and data- security, based on zero-trust principles, while being transparent in organization and technology. We stay politically neutral.
